sections.title: What it really costs
sections.intro: Monthly running costs, how the fees compare, and the one-off costs of buying.

items.head: Repair fund ¥20,080/month = ¥250/m²
items.detail: MLIT guideline for a building like this (under 20 floors, floor area < 5,000 m²): average ¥335/m², ⅔ of buildings ¥235–430. At the guideline average this flat would pay ≈ ¥26,900/month (+¥6,820). A fund below the guideline usually means future increases or a one-off levy (一時金).
items.cmp: Peers built ±5 years (605 watchlist condos): median ¥201/m², middle half ¥171–268 → this flat is at the 68th percentile.
items.ask: Please share the 長期修繕計画 and the current repair-fund balance. Are increases or a 一時金 planned?

items.head: Management fee ¥11,720/month = ¥146/m² (委託(巡回))
items.detail: Small buildings cost more per flat; staffed (常駐) management costs more than visiting (巡回).
items.cmp: Peers of similar age: median ¥160/m² → 36th percentile (605 condos)

items.head: ≈ ¥200,607/month before parking and property tax
items.detail: Loan ¥168,807 (100% of price, 35 years, 1.00% variable — the Apartments tab default) + fees ¥31,800
items.ask: What was the last 固定資産税・都市計画税 bill for this unit?

items.head: One-off buying costs ≈ ¥3,833,400–¥5,029,400
items.detail: Agent fee (仲介手数料, 3% + ¥60k + tax) ¥2,039,400 · plus registration tax and scrivener, loan fees and guarantee, fire + earthquake insurance, stamp duty, pro-rated property tax and fees: typically 3–5% of the price. Budget for renovation separately.

sections.title: Earthquake safety

items.head: Built 1999-08 — current seismic standard (新耐震)
items.detail: The rule depends on the building-permit date (from June 1981); completion from spring 1983 is almost always new-standard.

items.head: Structure: SRC, 9 floors
items.detail: RC/SRC are the norm for condos.

items.head: 30-year chance of shaking ≥ 6-lower here: 91% (≥ 6-upper: 43%)
items.detail: ≥ 5-upper: 100%. Modern buildings are designed for this; the risk is contents, lifts, pipes and the days without water or power.
items.cmp: Study areas (population-weighted, ≥ 6-lower): median 59%, range 24–89% → rank 78 of 78 from the safest

items.head: Ground: 三角州・海岸低地 — shaking amplified ×2.68
items.detail: Soft ground amplifies shaking (AVS30 126 m/s; about 1.6 or more counts as soft). Ask how the building is founded (piles to bearing stratum?).
items.ask: What kind of foundation does the building have (支持層までの杭基礎)?

src: J-SHIS 地震ハザードステーション

sections.title: Water and ground
sections.intro: Depth bands are the maximum assumed scenario (想定最大規模) at SUUMO's map point; SUUMO's point is approximate, so the worst value within ~100 m is shown too.

items.head: River flood: 3 m or more at the point
items.detail: The flat is on floor 1: it could be flooded, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Storm surge: 3 m or more at the point
items.detail: The flat is on floor 1: it could be flooded, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Liquefaction tendency: high
items.detail: Landform: 盛土地･埋立地 on 自然堤防 (国土地理院). Condo towers on piles usually stand, but roads, pipes, gas and sewers around them can fail for weeks (as in Urayasu 2011).
items.ask: Was the building or site damaged in 2011 (東日本大震災)? Ground improvement?

items.head: Area context (Adachi)
items.cmp: 97% of residents live in some water zone · 70% on high-liquefaction ground · 0.0% in landslide zones

items.head: Old maps
items.detail: Check what the site was before (sea, paddy, river) on 今昔マップ; past disaster records and 大規模盛土 maps come with the MLIT API key.

sections.intro: Energy labels are only required for new buildings (from April 2024): used flats almost never show them, so proxies are used.

items.detail: Era is only a hint: condos were not required to meet the energy standard until 2025.

items.head: Window type not stated
items.detail: In condos the window frames are common property: you usually cannot replace them yourself; inner windows (内窓) are allowed and subsidised.

items.head: Mortgage tax credit: eligible
items.detail: Built 1982 or later ✓ · registered area ≥ 50 m² ✓. Without an energy certificate a used home falls in the basic tier: 0.7% of the loan balance up to ¥20M for 10 years (max ¥140k/year). With a 省エネ基準適合 certificate it is 13 years; ZEH-level / 長期優良 raises the cap to ¥35M.
